reviews.text: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44181848/] 【更多适合Steam Deck的好游戏推荐，请关注GPD掌机鉴赏家！】[/url] 作为近年来在独立游戏领域频频发力的心动游戏，其发行的产品总能在玩法或品质上给人惊喜，《遗物守护者》再次印证了“心动发行，必属精品”的印象。 这款由Mystrigger开发的像素策略塔防游戏，核心创新在于打破了传统塔防的静态布局模式。玩家扮演的萌系勇者弗兰能够随时搬运防御塔，实现“热插拔”式的动态布防。当某条防线告急，立即抽调其他路线的塔防支援；甚至有漏网之鱼突破重围时，你还能扛着塔追着怪物补刀，这种设计极大地提升了游戏的策略深度与操作上限。 游戏内容丰富度令人满意，5大主题区域、23个关卡提供了超过15小时的冒险旅程。5类基础防御塔可进阶为15种形态各异的高阶英灵塔，而麦叽族巫女帕尼的9种化身更是能在战局危急时扭转乾坤。 游戏中的BOSS战设计颇具匠心，有些需要你及时移动防御塔躲避触手攻击并趁机反击，甚至隐藏着“上上下下左右左右”这样的经典彩蛋操作。 《遗物守护者》用可爱的像素画风、创新的玩法机制和充实的关卡内容，再次证明了心动在挑选独立游戏上的独到眼光。如果你既是塔防爱好者又是颜值控，这款游戏绝对值得你趁着首发折扣入手。

My aim in writing a review is to provide guidance to readers who are looking to buy the game and want to know how it fared with people who have played it. Secondarily, I want to write an analysis of the game and how I felt about it, which can support the first goal. “Relic Garden” can be classified as a remake of “Kingdom Rush”. The major structure is the same. There have been other “copies”, such as “Oriental Dynasty”, which is a classic in itself. These games usually fuse elements of other well known tower defense games to make them more interesting. I am very hesitant to be negative about Relic Garden because I know how much work it takes to produce a game like this, especially if it trying to emulate a past classic. It is a valiant attempt to be another Kingdom Rush, but it isn’t even close. If you have played and liked the Kingdom Rush series, you may enjoy this game too, despite its limitations. If you didn’t play Kingdom Rush series, I would recommend you try them first because they are much better and superior in every way - art design, balance, re-playability etc. So, what is not right with this one? There are several factors. I will talk about a few of them. First, it has a very odd and frustrating way to install and upgrade towers. There is a little character that needs to first go to a central location, pick up a tower, and then go to the site where you want to install the tower, and again go there if you want to upgrade it. This has no “fun value”, nor does it create any clever strategies. It can be set to not have to go to a central location to pick up a tower which improves the game a little, but why not have that as the default? Or not have the little character at all? The second issue is that it requires this character to be moved using keyboard commands. That makes it slow and not what most TD game players are used to. It causes frustration. Although there are many flaws, I will come to my last mention. There is a redundancy in how hard the game can be made. There is a place in the lower left corner where you can set your strength very high and the enemies strength low. You can win. Or you can also choose the “Kingdom Rush” style difficulty between easy-...-impossible. These two settings have a redundancy that makes the game less of a challenge and represents poor game design choices.

Let me preface this by saying this game is amazing. Easy 8/10. It’s fun, unique, funny, has great heart, and has a ton of heart. But But there are definitely some things keeping it from being a 9/10 or even a 1/10. These can be best summarized by its Spell/Hero system, how Fran operates, and other jank, missed potential, and strange decision choices. [h1] Spells & Heroes [/h1] Relic Guardians clearly takes inspiration from Kingdom Rush. That's not a bad thing, its an iconic TD series and inspired entire games like Relic Guardians itself. [h3] How Does Kingdom Rush do it? [/h3] (using KRO/KRV since thats a pretty consistent system). You get Three spells. [list] [*] An AoE spell to clear groups. [*] A Reinforcement spell to summon soldiers and stall enemies. [*] A Hero spell unique to your hero which can do anything. [/list] In addition, you get the Hero themselves, who has a single passive and four skills, which themselves can be automatically activated skills, or passive skills. This is a great system. The two global spells give you consistent utility regardless of what you use, and the Heroes extensive kits of a spell, passive, and their four skills makes them all hold their own weight well. [h3] How Does Relic Guardian do it? [/h3] Global Spells do not exist. All you have is what your Hero has. So what do Heroes have? Heroes have three Skills which can be either a: Player-activated spell, a automatically activated skill, or a passive skill. This... doesn't work well. Besides only giving the player a fraction of what KR does, the Players toolkit is heavily dependent on the hero. Some heroes have very strong Spells, while others have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ one or barely have spells at all. And a passive taking an entire skill slot is EVIL when KR knows to relegate that to its own thing and not draw away from the core kit. What this means for gameplay is that you’re not picking heroes because they’re fun, or because you like how they feel; you’re picking them based 99% on which has the most efficient skills, and its definitely NOT the one that has an entire Skill dedicated to how it operates (only appearing next to Fran or towers), or the one that has a Skill dedicated to picking a place to spawn units from their 2nd Skill, instead of just spawning them. And the worst part? The first hero has an AoE and Reinforcement spell just like Kingdom Rush, proving the devs know how vital that system is. Too bad its lost if you switch off her. Also, moving path-heroes has a cooldown. Evil. [h1] Fran The (Builder) [/h1] But wait! We have a second playable character, Fran, the Helper! What can she do? She can move, build, sell, and upgrade towers, and also interact with levels. And that’s it. She doesn't attack, doesn't buff allies or towers, doesn't have any skills, spells, passives, perks, etc. What the ♥♥♥♥? you might as well be playing as a construction crew. It’s wild. The game gives you full control of this character and then refuses to let her contribute in any meaningful way. You just stand around and pick your nose while your three-skill hero is fighting for their life. [h1] What Could Be [/h1] Then, just when you’ve given up hope, the game throws you a bone. In Chapter 3, you suddenly get global spells which you can use no matter who your Hero is. Then in Chapter 4, Fran finally obtains a sword which she can attack enemies with, and also can brew potions for different effects to herself, allies, enemies, or the environment. It's awesome! AND THEN THEY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DISAPPEAR. The instant the levels end, they're gone. Why introduce something this good only to delete it? It’s like the devs said, “Hey, here’s what fun feels like. Okay bye!” These shouldn't have been gimmicks. They should've been things from the get-go or permanent additions later in the game. I understand wanting unique gimmicks in levels and chapters but making them CORE THINGS THAT KR AND OTHER TD GAMES HAVE DONE FOR A DECADE wasn't the play. [h1] What If You Lost The Only Thing You Have? [/h1] The only control the Player has over the game besides Fran and Towers is located entirely within the Heroes. So the game would never take them away, right? It does. Twice. 2-5 and 5-3 both remove your hero for story reasons. THIS IS ♥♥♥♥! Both happen in levels where the Global spells and Fran's sword/potions are gone, meaning you have zero active options. It's like the stars aligned to ruin your life. 2-5 was cancerous. 5-3 was better but only because it re-introduces Pani at the end and also is nowhere as hard. [h1] Smaller Problems & Missed Potential [/h1] Besides above, the smaller (but still noticeable) stuff. [h3] 1-5 Jank [/h3] 1-5 drags like crazy. The boss has tentacles you need to destroy to damage it, but the game never tells you that. Worse, the tentacles despawn if not killed fast enough, so you think you’re doing something wrong for ten minutes straight. [h3] 2-5 Jank [/h3] 2-5 seemed amazing. A dramatic arena fight between Pani and Frieed, but then Frieed just gets defeated. The challenge version actually makes Frieed appear on the track with different attacks and a boss health bar. It’s so much better. Why isn’t THAT in the main level? It could've been a sort of thing where the game swaps between Pani/Frieed in the arena, and returning Pani to your control but Frieed pushes down the path. [h3] Chapter 5 Enemy Variety [/h3] Chapter 5 is the final area in the game yet has less enemies than any other area by a huge margin. I think barely half of what Chapter 1 or 2 has? Very strange. [h3] 5-3 Jank [/h3] 5-3, similarly to 2-5, is very cool. The final witch is a very intimidating enemy and her first phase keeps you on your toes. And then the second phase happens and mmmm. The Witch goes into her super form and lowers your health to one, but Pani breaks into her own super form for the final battle. And then that's kinda it? I dont think the witch gets any stronger as the fight goes on, so what starts awesome becomes kinda lame as you just chip away at her huge health pool. The enemy backup is also very weak so its ironically much easier than the first phase. [h3] The Ending [/h3] After beating the final Witch, she dies like every other boss without much fanfare. Then you just get a little animation of the world going to normal like someone flipped a switch, and credits roll. It was so anticlimactic that I thought it was a fakeout for a third phase. But no, it actually just ends. Wheres the showcase of the aftermath? The celebration of the Whickens? What Fran and Pani do? What happens to the other allies and enemies in the world, like the natives, or Frieed who's still alive? I'm aware all this here is just my own opinion but, come on. Again, even KR from a decade ago did all this. [h3] Tower Talents [/h3] There's a grand total of three tower Talents that affect more than 2 towers. Every other upgrade only affects one or two towers. Very specific for no reason. Any Towers you actually like cant get much development. [h1] Closing Thoughts [/h1] Relic Guardian has the bones of something incredible. The art, humor, and creativity are all there. But it constantly undercuts itself with uneven design, missing systems, and mechanics that vanish right when they start to get interesting. If the game gets updates that are more than just minor changes/content, or a sequel in the future, here's what I personally suggest: [list] [*] Heroes having more than three skills, and if they have a SMALL passive, perhaps relegate it to a dedicated 'passive' spot instead. [*] Broad tower upgrades getting more love. Specific upgrades are nice, but when they're the only upgrades, it kinda sucks. [*] Fran getting more presence. Let her do LITERALLY ANYTHING other than just tower/level stuff. I'm not asking for her to be a second hero (would be cool tho), but just for her to do SOMETHING more. [*] Global spells/skills. If not a dedicated system, then see Fran content above. [/list]

《遗物守护者》是一款玩法革新的塔防游戏，打破了传统塔防的模式桎梏，让防御塔能被玩家扛在肩上满场飞奔，也能利用英雄、士兵和防御塔构建各种环境变化，进一步提升游戏的塔防策略。本作游戏凭借颠覆性的动态布防机制与像素化的萌系画风，掀起了一场塔防革命。 [h1]动态塔防机制[/h1] 《遗物守护者》的创新核心机制在于防御塔实时迁移模式。玩家需在祭坛消耗资源生成防御塔基座，随后将其部署至预设的阵地坑位上，就可以让其发挥作用了。与传统塔防游戏位置固定的模式不同，本作允许玩家随时回收防御塔并重新配置，且这一过程无冷却限制，玩家可以随时根据场上的战况动态调整。这种设计提升了资源利用率，更大大提升了塔防策略，动态管理塔防战场。尤其是在某些BOSS战中，BOSS会对防御塔进行攻击造成伤害，玩家可以随时动态调整防御塔位置，躲避BOSS的致命攻击，回收防御塔，并在BOSS陷入僵直的时候放置防御塔进行反击。 [h1]只会卖萌不会攻击的勇者更可怕[/h1] 游戏中玩家将在塔防地图中扮演麦叽族勇者弗兰，作为游戏的主角，她的设定堪称“反传统英雄模板”。她不会释放华丽技能，没有任何攻击能力，却拥有强力的卖萌能力和实用能力。搬运防御塔是主角的特殊能力之一，也是前面所说的核心机制。除此之外，主角还拥有抱大腿卖萌的能力，扑向敌人，并减速敌人，看上去非常滑稽的但是在战场中却非常实用，深刻改变了塔防游戏的互动逻辑。 除去卖萌的主角之外，游戏也拥有类似防御塔的输出类强大英雄，通过使用强大的技能对敌人造成伤害，也可以为周围的防御塔提供BUFF，使防御塔的能力获得提升。将英雄技能与防御塔进行联动可以提供爆炸一般的输出效果，也是游戏的主要核心战术，是游戏的主要策略。 [h1]动态挑战的地图机制[/h1] 游戏的战场地图，每张地图都独一无二的，均设计有独特机制与隐藏要素，例如充电桩的设计，让两边的防御塔等级之和达到6级就可以激活陷阱，对经过的敌人造成伤害。有的地图还包含互动陷阱，点击火车轨道可召唤列车撞击敌群，或是唤醒沉睡青蛙可释放清除敌人的激光束。这些机制增加了地图探索的乐趣，更要求玩家根据地形调整战术，进一步增强了游戏的策略性。 [table][td][b]欢迎关注我们 [/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/10591434/]突突突发糖辣！[/url] [/td][/table]

Decent game on paper but the over-reliance on moving towers instead of just giving your character a way to interact with the battlefield feels really boring. Everything feels like it was bottle-necked around them wanting to have you play 'your part' while being in the field, but all it really does it drag out interactions. To place a tower anywhere i have to waddle back to the summoning circle and carry it somewhere every time. Upgrading feeling clunky and most upgrades don't feel significant besides the final one giving an ability that auto-goes off occasionally. Heroes feel anywhere from Weak to Insanely strong, the second hero you unlock trivializes entire sections with her abilities in comparison to the starting hero who is also a tower and takes up a tower slot on the map which is annoying since she isn't very strong. Enemy Variety feels mediocre. Honestly if they just removed the whole 'summoning circle' aspect or gave your character something to actually attack with (Maybe replace the worthless attack the guys at the end of every track have that is not worth getting with an attack for your character) it'd be enjoyable, but other than that the annoyance of it all and extreme reliance on tower repositioning feels bad. Can't say i'm much of a fan. Otherwise there's some other letdowns, the Music is Mediocre at best, the Tower Variety is bad (Physical and Magical Damage, each has a single target and aoe version and 1 type of barracks for troop blocking.) Enemy Variety also didn't feel very good with the sole threat being Flyers and nothing else only because Towers don't have targeting priority, so they waste time hitting ground troops that aren't a threat (or worse the randomly spawning enemy who drops coins, i love losing lives because this random stupid enemy spawns and distracts my ranged towers from hitting crucial fliers, yippee!!) Another big gripe is level length feeling just way too long. Even with clicking the waves instantly they take ages with nothing even coming close to getting through on Hard until Fliers or the Final Wave. Losing a life that late feels absolutely horrid. Also just a nitpick but the UI seems really unecessary. There's buttons for UI elements that takes you to a different page from the level select map, but the buttons are also at the bottom of the level select map, making the other map for only upgrades and stuff really pointless and just an annoying extra click everytime to get off of it. If you're looking for some positives the graphics are very nice and the maps feel cool with all the little clickable easter eggs. The Towers seem to have interesting upgrades unlocked via challenge mode but i lost interest after unlocking a single one towards the end of my playtime. Talents seem cool as well but after losing a life in a 15+ minute level because the upgrade for the guys at the end of the track was so horrifically bad I was skeptical of a lot of them. Refunding this, although i can acknowledge it might just be me, give it a try if it interests you but it didn't scratch my tower defense itch in the slightest.

Kind of just a janky game. Missing weird stuff here and there. Overall just an inferior version of the kingdom rush games, with a story that makes no sense. The gimmick of having to go to towers and move them around isn't used almost ever as an actual mechanic, and its usually just annoying because of the way its implemented. upgrading things you have to stand next to them, but you don't just click the thing, so you can click on one tower, but if your character is next to another tower, it upgrades that one instead. Also your upgrades don't just happen, you can put the coins into the tower partially, so you can absolutely get F'd if something needs an upgrade, but you are standing next to something else jut a little too much and it gets half the points and doesn't upgrade and now you are stuck with a half upgraded tower you didn't mean to put coins into. Its super annoying and pointless. The balance is all backwards too which is another issue in and of itself. Towers don't have upgrades in the meta progression. Instead you have to pick between some trade off upgrades that usually get you killed because they are so bad. Some towers also just suck. No reason to pick some things that don't put out dps when the other upgrade path is better in every way. Do you like annoying boss fights? This game has that. Interactable map units/upgades also suck terribly. You work towards activating something and it ends up doing as much damage as half a tier 1 tower, or its a one time thing. Placement spots also suck. The game looks charming, but its just a cheap rip off of kingdom rush, so do yourself a favor and play those games instead.

很有意思的一款休闲塔防，以下有几点我认为是这游戏的可圈可点之处。 1：游戏中帕尼的不同形态以及防御塔的变种都各有千秋，在解锁完善收集的过程中不止一次给我耳目一新的惊喜感，且一塔多形态的设计也为同一防御塔提供了多种不同流派，不同针对的bd，能够使大多数防御塔都有出场的机会而不是图鉴中的背景板（这点虽难能可贵但也不算完美，仍然有些塔是其他防御塔的准下位或上位，不过官方也发布公告：后续会进行平衡调整，那么敬请期待吧)。 2：游戏考虑到了不同水平玩家的需求与体验贴心地给了场外金手指以便玩家实时调整难度，这点可大加赞赏(就个人而言哪怕游戏的最高难度，其体感体验下来算是中等水平）。 3：令我意外的是游戏的每一章节都有花费心思设计贴合敌人特点以及增添趣味的特殊机制，怪物之间的联动在还算合理的过程中也为通关过程增补了不少紧张感和刺激感（点名批评kr5）。 4：游戏中的挑战关虽然称作挑战，但鄙人认为叫做“体验关”更为恰当，整体难度与平常关卡相差不大，但因为塔变种的解锁让玩家在通关的过程中改变用塔惯性从而体验到别样的重玩乐趣，这也未尝不是一种另辟蹊径的挑战 以上，是我玩这款游戏中感受最深的部分，还有些许我没有提及，但我相信：入手这款游戏的你在游玩的过程中一定能够发现并感受到的。言尽于此，我很高兴业界哺育了如此优秀的塔防游戏，游玩的过程我感到很愉快。

Very cute game! There's a lot of love and attention sprinkled throughout, and a lot of references to other games or pop culture things. There's a fair amount of variety for the tower upgrades (sidegrades?) though they're optional unlocks on the challenge stages. 5x3 towers, 4 forms (base, 1, 2 3), bring 5x2 per stage. Chapters also have themes and special mechanics which is really refreshing. I was also amazed at how many hero choices there were! And all so cute and stylish! Everything is so beautifully animated, from enemy to tower to stage. Only con is that the game is rather short if you make use of the 2x speed button, and you will want to for some stages. I wish there were something like bonus stages with asset flips, or a easy to make (for the artist) crayon style dream bonus chapter with mixes of enemies. A map maker like Bloons would also add a ton of longevity. Still, no regrets here. Progress from the demo does not carry over, but the demo is very complete otherwise, chapter 1.

This game is genuinely good, one of the better tower defense games I've played. There are legitimately difficult sections that require a lot of thought. you have a lot of tower variety both inside and outside of levels that allow for a lot of powerful synergies that are needed for some of the challenge levels. Aesthetically the game is colourful and cute. Game feels smooth on higher speeds. It looks a little clunky on lower speeds but that might be my eyes playing tricks on me. If you're a fan of the kingdom rush series I would recommend this game even though they aren't that comparable. The game's main sources of micro are moving around to place and move towers around with your character as well as using your heroes abilities. Your hero unit Pani can be moved independently through a teleport but this is on a timer, which generally means less hero micro and more strategy. I don't know why, but I really like the games hero system. I would highly recommend.

If you want an easy playthrough this is probably great, for me who wanted a challenge this wasn't fun. The game feels heavily designed around the strategy of throwing towers around. There is no other reason to have a slow cumbersome builder that makes the most basic tasks like building towers and upgrading them a time consuming chore. I get it, if the game had a high level of user experience and you could just build, upgrade and teleport towers around with the click of a button it would be hard to balance. They balanced it around making everything a pain instead, which for me was not fun, For example the second I notice things are starting to go badly I want the tools to fix the situation. If my left lane seems to be killing things too slowly I can't do anything about it in time. I need to run to some circle, get some tower, choose a place, run and throw it there and while all of this is going on I can't do anything else. I can't upgrade any towers and I can't build any more than the one I had to rush to put out. Either way its not enough and now I am probably starting to leak on the other lane instead. For me this did not feel satisfying to play
